tei:titleStmt.tei:title: קְדוּשְׁתָּאוֹת לְשַׁבָּת זָכוֹר
Qedushtaot for Shabbat Zakhor, by Elazar ben Qallir

tei:div.tei:head: Qedushtaot for Shabbat Zakhor, by Elazar ben Qallir

tei:lg.tei:l: Blessed are You,
o Cause, our God
and God of our ancestors
God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob.
The Deity,
great and mighty and awesome;
the almighty Deity,
who well repays kindness,
and possesses all,
and remembers the kindnesses of ancestors
and sends a redeemer to their descendants
for Their Name’s sake, in love.
Sovereign,
and Rescue
and Shield —
Reshut
By the counsel of sages and scholars,
and the study of knowledge-understanders,
let me open my mouth in song and cheer
to thank and praise the countenance of the Dweller on High.
Magen
Always I will recall the remembrance of acts
By these days remembered and kept as facts.
Creeping out from among the snakes on its ribcage,
Disgusting to recall, rotting in rage.
Erupting from tumbleweed and thistle, the thorn
From age to age would whirl on, unworn.
Gloomed he his father’s eyes by iniquity to recall.
He sinned against his mother; let it not fall!
In rage he tore, destroying the womb;
Jerking his conceiver not to enjoy the bedroom.
Kin third-generation was appointed vengeance’s sin:
Let them hastily fight those who took the bread in.
Making the four-hundred parasang walk he tread,
Nomadically traveling with a net to spread.
On his way from Seir, he hid it laid out,
Planning, for shame! to mutilate the tired and worn out.
Quite enraged at the disrupted birthright, he acted
Resolving to sell the holy flock for slavery protracted.
Stylus-engraved is his disgrace to remember
To be the first nation to be scratched with “Remember!”
Upon remembering the night-divider, the Surveyor
Vitiated in slipperiness the wood and root of the slayer.
Exchange for strangling those yonder delayed,
Zealously They demand we recall ‘Amaleq’s raid.

tei:l.tei:note: In most modern Ashkenazi practice, the catenae of verses inserted after the first three piyyutim are not recited.

tei:lg.tei:l: As it is written:
Remember what ‘Amaleq did to you
on the way as you went out from Egypt. (Deuteronomy 25:17)
And it is said:
And he saw ‘Amaleq
and raised his tune and said:
first of nations is ‘Amaleq,
but its end will be final destruction. (Numbers 24:20)
And it is said:
The memory of the righteous is for a blessing,
and the name of the wicked rots. (Proverbs 10:7)
And it is said:
Let iniquity to his father be recalled to the Cause;
and do not erase the sin at his mother! (Psalms 109:14)
And it is said:
And these days are recalled and done in each and every generation,
each and every family,
each and every state,
each and every city,
and these days of Purim will not pass from amongst the Jews,
and their memory will not end from their seed. (Esther 9:28)
And it is said:
There is no memory of the former,
and so too the latter that will be
will have no memory,
as they will be at the latter. (Ecclesiastes 1:11)
At the latter going out among them, he prevailed,
for the cloud excluded the tribe that trailed.
None will escape when they are erased;
They shield the people shielded and saved in haste.
Blessed are You, o Cause, shield of Abraham.
You are mighty forever, Master,
You bring life to the dead, greatly saving.
You turn the wind and send down the rain.
You provide for life in kindness,
reviving the dead in great mercy,
lift the fallen,
heal the sick,
free the bound,
and keep faith with sleepers in the dust.
Who is like You, Master of Powerful Acts,
and who can be compared to You?
Sovereign, who brings death and life
and causes salvation to sprout.
And trusted are You to revive the dead —
Meḥayeh
Zenithal ones, yet in Sin, were enclothed
Yes, in finery wrapped, as befits the betrothed.
Exactly when taking the gift of flame
Weak at Rephidim, their hands became lame.
Villainously he horded up all his horde
Upon their camp to do crime as they gathered toward.
To those whose feet ascended from the deep-sea reeds,
Sought he to cut them down like canes and reeds.
Roaming, he flew at them on three occasions,
Quickly going by the descendants of five nations.
Prudent was the simple when the mocker was struck,
On this, to join the princely people he had the luck.
Notoriously, the mocker set up a highway
Mashing down my young men with behavior astray.
Looking to defile my rounded thighs,
Knocked up the treasure the way they despise.
Jealous, like his grandfather’s grudge, he was hidden
Initially coming out from being hidden.
He broke out the second time with a flaming sword,
Going forth the third time, from our sin, aboveboard.
From the Sheshkhite’s rule over the ruling folk,
Encamped he to inform on refugees as he spoke.
Declaring, “Come, let us destroy those much maligned,”
By the same way he had anciently tailed those behind.
As it is written:
...who came upon you on the way
and tailed you, all those behind after you,
as you were tired and weary,
and had no fear of God. (Deuteronomy 25:18)
And it is said:
They said, “Come, let us destroy them from nationhood,
and let the name of Israel no more be recalled.” (Psalms 83:5)
And it is said:
You strike the mocker
and the simple becomes prudent;
but reprove the intelligent
and he will understand knowledge (Proverbs 19:25)
And it is said:
Hey, all these the Deity does,
twice, three times to a man. (Job 33:29)
And it is said:
The insolent dug pits for me,
which is not per Your Teaching. (Psalms 119:85)
And it is said:
Turn back to them recompense, Cause,
as per their handiwork. (Lamentations 3:64)
And it is said,
Your hand is enough for all Your enemies;
Your right hand is enough for Your foes. (Psalms 21:9)
Your foes will wear their disgrace,
As they rejoiced at my fall out of thirst at that place.
When You are wrapped in Your ten garments of grace,
Rain down life to treat the limping one’s face.
Blessed are You, o Cause, who revives the dead.
Meshalesh
As my tormentors’ zealous foes, the heirs of Seir,
Brood of “yonder children of Seir,”
Charged with their straw, my fire to sear
Exultantly plowing my city clear.
Did You not recall the nation great?
Why, then, did You remember their sinful state?
Exchanging the bannered hosts for a price of no weight,
Vine’s blood and whores as the holy’s rebate!
For the Edomites who burned the Sanctum, recall,
Unpleasant ones who battered the wall.
“Get it to the foundation, let it fall, let it fall!”
They gaped open their mouths and shouted in gall.
Hence, You, before whom none forget
Store their rage forever, not to forget
In that they did not know to do as they were let,
Ratify their book for the day they’ll regret!
Just as the law quotes, it demonstrates
Keenly it will be put in mind, lest the memory abates
Let Them come strive with them on that very date;
Marking Your people not to forget per Your mandate!
As it is written:
And when the Cause your God makes you rest
from all your enemies around in the land
that the Cause your God is giving you as an estate to inherit,
you will erase the memory of ‘Amaleq from under heaven;
do not forget! (Deuteronomy 25:19)
And it is said:
Remember, Cause,
the children of Edom,
on the day of Jerusalem,
saying “Raze it, raze it
down to its foundation!” (Psalms 137:7)
And it is said:
Tear after them in rage and destroy them
from under the Cause’s heavens. (Lamentations 3:66)
Jeering, he set a wounding tripline
Upon the troops sealed with the covenant sign.
Deemed measure for measure, payback condign,
As knowledge that at the chosen deadline
He will be accounted for by the Cause divine.
As it is written:
Thus says the Cause of Forces:
I have accounted for what ‘Amaleq did to Israel,
setting upon them on the path
as they went up from Egypt. (I Samuel 15:2)
And it is said:
Did you not hear from afar?
I did that, from days of yore I crafted it,
now I have brought it about,
and it has happened; to ruin
to desolate heaps fortified cities. (Isaiah 37:26, II Kings 19:25)
And it is said:
The dead shall not live,
the ghosts shall not rise,
thus You accounted for them and wiped them out,
ending all their memory. (Isaiah 26:14)
And it is said:
The Cause reigns forever;
your God, Zion, from generation to generation;
praise Yah! (Psalms 146:10)
And You are holy, enthroned on Israel’s praise. (Psalms 22:4)
El Na
Deity, please!
By the phrase that You made Your rememberers recall, “remember”
By that very phrase they make You recall – “please remember!”
And if they, mortals, breached the covenant they should remember,
You are a Deity, not a mortal, so why don’t You remember?
By this I know that You have it in You to remember,
But my soul sinks in me until You remember, remember!
And what strength do I have to wait for the final “Remember?”
And what patience to draw out my soul until You remember?
If not for my sake You will remember,
Then for Your own, and for Jerusalem’s, remember.
The law, the testimony not to be forgotten, remember!
Saying “If I forget you, Jerusalem” now, it You must remember!
And account for the tormentor’s painful afflictions and remember;
Shut his mouth; let him stumble like one too drunk to remember.
And never again sell off those entitled the firstborn member,
Bought for a letekh and kor, as Your glory I remember.
And I will, as You wish, remember, with the portion of “Remember!”
Ḥay v-Qayyam
Living and enduring, awesome and exalted and holy!
Expressly Thorn Thornson would trim off the tail,
with shattering speech, assailed ones to assail.
Laughing came the leerer, but was staggered, to wail:
“Fire arrows, like an eagle that swoops on a quail!”
As the cloud broke overhead to exclude some guys,
he started off and attacked, with a back-plowing reprise.
Zenith he was entitled, first of nations to despise,
The arch-traitor whose viper would to the choice cypress gallows rise.
As he ran he came across the tired and weary on the way,
Saying, “Not this way,” they erred in the wild desert way.
Reaching at the thighs’ curve, at the snake on the way,
He cut down at each crossroad passers-by along the way.
He flew, flying quick, from the python crept from its pit,
Known from the snake’s root he would hoof it.
And he whispered, muttering his birthchart to calculate it,
but his wizardry weakened him to silently submit.
Quelled was by with his own magic! He was misled.
He held back the day, stopping the sun ahead.
As shame was his portion, rest did not bestead,
Lingering until sunrise, he and his force to be struck dead.
Lashing out, gnashing teeth, he screamed words abhorred,
Smelling the stench, he unsheathed his sword.
Lopping off the circumcised parts, he threw them upward,
and at the Name sweeter than oil spat a hateful word.
Instructed Yah the All-Atoning to he with a fawn’s look,
Scatter his memory like ash! Write this memory in a book!
Recounted is his shamedness
in the Teaching, Prophets, and Writings,
in this very book,
That he be erased from the book and not written with those written for life in the book.
Deity, please,
forever are You adored
and forever are You sanctified
and forever and aye will You reign and be exalted,
the Deity, sovereign, awesome, high and holy,
for You are the Sovereign,
Sovereign of sovereigns,
whose sovereignty is eternal;
tell Their awesomenesses,
recount Their strength,
glorify Their forces,
sanctify Them, exalt Them,
cheer, song, and laudation,
mighty praises of Their glory.
And so — Remember what ‘Amaleq did to you. (Deuteronomy 25:17)
And erase his name and memory,
and we will erase his memory
from him being recalled
in memory, Holy!
Since he did not remember,
and he is considered like a stranger,
not to be recalled
in memory, Holy!
Remember a man who made the father untimely die;
by killing and stealing, in adultery he would lie;
causing five years to be taken from the life of the guy.
And erase...
Remember boorishly he disdained acts of respect,
Contemning his brother paying his elder last respects,
Deemed one withholding from his friend respect.
Since he...
Remember carnally he stripped a woman in the field,
Doing bloodshed as he came back from the field;
Erred the heart of the father meditating in the field.
And erase...
Remember deferring with a deaf ear,
Eschewing the birthright for a cup of staggering fear,
Flipping off the yoke, from circumcision he did veer.
Since he...
Remember erratic was that man’s path, and strange;
For he dimmed his father’s light in smoke of worship strange,
Getting into his heart to fraternal cruelty arrange.
And erase...
Remember for he would get screwed like a girl
Going to such depravity with the heart of a churl,
His warriors will be pained like the heart of a girl.
Since he...
Remember gross and tainted evildoers’ seed!
He set out with “Aha!” to make the smooth one bleed.
In pride he hid for his brother a net to mislead.
And erase...
Remember he from whom the ‘Amaleqite did sprout,
Invading to ruin my portion like locusts throughout,
Jeapordizing the great to lick my blood all-out.
Since he...
Remember insane, lacking any sense,
Jabbing at my people to destruction thence,
Karma thus suggests destruction as recompense.
And erase...
Remember jackass-like, unyoked the southerner,
Kit and speech he changed to be Arad’s governor,
Looting captives as he rebelled and shuddered her.
Since he...
Remember knuckleheadedly returning to his folly
Looking to ally with Midian for another volley,
Moving fast, Jerubbeshet brought his evil to finale.
And erase...
Remember “leave no seed, uproot!
May none leave him a branch or root!”
Now the Qishite was punished for leaving him a root.
Since he...
Remember matters done by Agag the chained,
Nastily with his sword, women he profaned.
Ostriches ate his hacked off bits, as was ordained.
And erase...
Remember noble Shaul, who to spare him agreed.
Out went his reign from among princes with this deed.
Pullulated the remnant to stand as a thorny weed.
Since he...
Remember overrunning Tsiqlag and the south.
Parked was ‘Amaleq in the land of the south.
Quite handsome, his slayer played pipe with his mouth.
And erase...
Remember persecutor who among Ammonites hid,
Quartered in Ein Gedi for its vineyards to be rid,
Ravage one another with the flaming sword they did!
Since he...
Remember quaking rage as he shook up the refugees,
Regarding the flight to Mt. Seir of my armies,
Seir’s towns’ vengeance he was zealous to appease.
And erase...
Remember rising at the pass to close on the runaways,
Standing to help my oppressors at the crossways,
To pursue and hand over to them my scattered strays.
Since he...
Remember springing up to the gates of heaven,
There he stormed, shouting “Who is mine in heaven?”
Upon which he reigned, swelling up to heaven.
And erase...
Remember to flatter the hypocrite’s kingdom he came,
Up went Shimshai whose sun eclipsed, per his name,
Vilifying the pure that their labor be made lame.
Since he...
Remember underwriter of ten thousand by weight
Virile was he, a hundred seeds he did germinate,
Wazirs ten of them he did delegate.
And erase...
Remember vouched he to destroy the five;
Whole year he set that the armed would not survive
Expired after seventy, on the fifty hanged, not alive.
Since he...
Silluq
And thus, to You holiness ascends,
For You are the Holy One and Savior of Israel.
God, do not silence Yourself!
At the mighty waters’ sound let Your voice be heard,
making heard and commanding Your people to acquire Your work —
“remember what he did to you,
who came upon you and cut you off,
and when the Cause your God makes you rest,
erase his name and memory!”
And they respond and say to You,
giving to You again what is Yours:
“Please, fulfill the word You spoke!”
As You commanded us to recall,
You must remember what they did to You!
Remember, Cause, the day of Your splendor,
when they self-aggrandizingly proclaimed, “What do You have here?”
They stuck out their penises to defile Your nostril!
Remember Your great throne of glory,
that they cut down and derided before You!
And they sent fire upon Your palace,
and laid waste to all Your borders,
and looted and pillaged the hangings of Your tent —
those of which You commanded should not come into the congregation!
They said, “Come, let us destroy them from nationhood for Your sake,
that no longer recalled shall be the name of Your glory;
You upon whom the hapless trust!
And more than what they did to us, they did to You.
To us they fought in the wilderness.
But to You they made war in settlements.
To us outside the camp they harrassed;
But to You within the camp they roared.
To us the cloud’s exiles they violated;
But to You the clouded purgation-cover they razed.
To us they cut down the cumulus-ejected,
But to You ascending to the cumulus they sought.
To us outside the barrier they rose,
But to You within and without they went in.
To us far from the place they charged,
But to You within Your place they laid waste.
To us outside our dwellings they cast us down,
But to You in Your set abode they cut down.
To us the covenant-sign they tore from us,
But to You ten covenantal nobilities they destroyed.
To us they rose as the humble’s hands rested,
But to You they raised their hanging hand against You.
To us they plotted and conspired in secret
But to You Your secret mount-angels they vilely removed.
And You, the Cause, forever are enthroned;
but he against You sits below.
Seizing wilderness and settlement,
“I and none like me!” thinking in his heart.
If You do not rise now and give heed,
with thirteen rising of calculated vengeance,
in terror and tartarus and trap to account for the inhabitant,
if not, like a stranger You would be considered!
But all who count and ennumerate and calculate
the final wonders, to understand and be calculated,
all his strength of mind would be forgotten,
and he would find no answer to be answered,
and hold silent, quiet from hearing.
But with faith he would settle his loins,
and set this on his heart,
and say, “Till They look down and see” and hearken.
But I am considered like a false witness,
always making it up,
and my soul is very afraid and astonished,
and You, Cause, how long will You see and be silent?
Remember Your destroyed Temple;
all who pass by are astonished.
When will You be lifted and exalted,
and fulfill the memory of Your mouth’s word —
with three eras to to stun ‘Amaleq,
with three deaths to darken their memory,
with three days of darkness to fade out their glow,
with seven days of rage to brand them,
with ten kinds of apostasy to render them guilty?
And just as they stopped the people from testifying to the Ten Commandments,
and the seven most ancient commandments,
thus let them be drunken with ten and seven harms.
And a divine voice should come out from the lofty abodes,
and proclaim in all the camps
the mention of these things to tell and answer:
“Do not recall the former;
understand the latter salvations,
and recall the memory of cheering!
‘Amaleq who came and corrupted the camps,
and accosted you before the daughters,
and gained a name for himself before the nations;
now look at this, to tell
how he is erased suddenly from all corners!
And the force on high in the lofty abodes
on which he used to rely as support
will account for them the iniquities,
to be counted over many days,
to calculate their calculations,
to throw them into the abhorrent underworld.
And the multitudinous nations and all the tongues
will raise a lament to the helper and helped —
“Stumbled is the helper; fallen the helped!” they lament.
And all works will know You did not forget,
and all creatures will understand that their name You made forgotten,
and Seir and its princes You thus disputed,
and ‘Amaleq and its potentates You punished,
and with them in judgment You argued.
But the people You remembered will be remembered,
because for good You remembered them,
and in memory of good with them You are recalled.
And those who recall the Cause
Will always say “greatened be the Cause!”
And thus will say the redeemed of the Cause:
“So may all Your enemies fall, Cause!:”
And those standing in the house of the Cause
And trusting in the Cause
And those planted in the house of the Cause
Will see the pleasantness of the Cause
And tell that none are holy like the Cause
For a merciful Deity is the Cause!
Content are all who revere the Cause.
It is good to thank the Cause.
It is good to trust in the Cause.
Cheer, righteous ones, in the Cause!
The voice of those saying “Give thanks to the Cause,”
For they are a seed blessed by the Cause.
This day was made by the Cause!
For a great Deity is the Cause!
Blessed be one who comes in the name of the Cause.
I will rejoice, rejoice in the Cause!
And if all the festivals will be nullified,
the days of Purim will not be nullified,
and their memory will not cease from those taken up;
and the redemptions will be remembered forever,
for joy and cheerful happiness.
The acts of God they will reveal,
and Their mighty deeds they will exalt,
and singers as dancers trilling
with ten kinds of ten-stringed lyres,
with citharas and lutes,
praising with ten kinds of praises,
celebrating with ten kinds of happiness.
And the most exalted holy snake-angels will ask them,
like a student asks his teacher,
“What has the Deity of deities done?”
For these ones will be on the inside,
and those ones will clear the way before them,
and those ones ones will face them from outside,
and these ones within and without,
in the shade of the Surveyor lodging,
and with the five reserved voices,
the preserved sound of cheer and salvation
hidden in the tents of the righteous,
who meditate on that which is more precious than pearls.
The singers will come first,
then afterwards the musicians,
to know how they play.
In the pride of protective scales,
under their shadow they will be shielded,
and in their pinions they will shield themselves.
As gatekeepers and guardians will they be set,
ready all day and all night,
to recall the holiness of the guardians of faith,
and to proclaim the memory of the nation keeping faith.
And by Israel’s name they will be referred,
and in threefold holinesses to the Holy they will devote —
two they set on the head of the children
and one they prepare for the head of their Sovereign.
And with all three they are prepared,
and a complete throne and complete name they prepare,
and with the threefold holiness they answer as of old, understanding,
calling one to another they direct,
and by the moniker of the holy name they call and refer:
As is written by Your prophet’s hand...

tei:note.tei:p: This brief reshut was not written by Qallir. It is inserted into the Ashkenazi rite here to justify the practice of inserting piyyutim.
A midrash found in multiple places, including Midrash Tanḥuma Ki Tetze 4:1, states that Isaac went blind from looking at Esau.
Midrash Tanḥuma Ki Tetze 4:1 states that in being born, Esau injured Rebecca’s uterus, leaving her unable to orgasm.
Midrash Tanḥuma Beshallaḥ 25:2 states ‘Amaleq had to travel four hundred parasangs to reach Israel.
Abraham, referencing the Covenant of the Pieces in Genesis 15
A translation of the divine name Shaddai, based on Bereshit Rabbah 46:3 (on Genesis 17:1) that the name means “the One who said ‘enough’ (dai).”
According to Midrash Tanḥuma Ki Tetze 10:1, the tribe of Dan, the hindmost tribe, was excluded from the cloud of glory on account of being idolators, and were thus the tribe that ‘Amaleq defeated.
Midrash Tanḥuma, Beshallaḥ 25:2 states that ‘Amaleq had to travel through five nations’ land to reach Israel.
Exodus 17, Deuteronomy 25, and I Samuel 15, according to B. Megillah 7a.
Midrash Tanḥuma, Beshallaḥ 25:4 states that ‘Amaleq could only attack because Israel’s hands had grown weak in the fulfillment of the mitzvot.
Jethro. Midrash Tanḥuma, Yitro 3:2 states that Jethro had heard about the destruction of ‘Amaleq before converting.
Midrash Tanḥuma, Beshallaḥ 25:2 states that ‘Amaleq commited male-on-male rape against Israel.
Nebuchadnezzar. Sheshakh is atbash cipher for Babylonia, a term used already in Jeremah 25:26.
Rephidim, where Israel had no water.
Find the midrash first found in Pesiqta d-Rav Kahana 22:5, but also found in Devarim Rabbah 2:37, which lists ten times Israel uses the language of “clothing” to praise God.
The tribe of Dan, which according to the midrash was the rearguard attacked by ‘Amaleq on account of not being protected by the clouds of glory, due to their tendency towards idol worship.

Moses. According to Midrash Tanḥuma, Beshallaḥ 28:1, ‘Amaleq calculated the best time to attack via astrology, and Moses stopped them by holding up the revolution of the sun and moon and rendering their predictions invalid.

According to Midrash Tanḥuma Ki Tetzei 9-10, this is the meaning of “he tailed you” (Deut. 25:18). The ‘Amaleqites cut off the penises of Israel and threw them upwards saying “You chose this! Take what You chose!”
Literally “the henna cluster.” Find Shabbat 88b on Song of Songs 1:14
Moses, who was humble, like a fawn.
In many texts, written יִמַּח שְׁמוֹ וְזִכְרוֹ — “his name and memory should be erased!” A common scribal mix-up between vav and yod.
Esau. According to Midrash Tanḥuma Ki Tetzei 4:1, Abraham lived five years fewer than Isaac because in those five years Esau committed two sins: sleeping with an engaged woman and killing someone
According to Pirkei d’Rabbi Eliezer 2:10, Esau despised the circumcision. The yoke refers to the Divine commandments.
According to Midrash Tanḥuma, Toldot 8, the smoke from Esau’s idol-worshipping wives made Isaac go blind.

A bit of casual homophobia here. There’s a worrying through-line of painting Esau and ‘Amaleq as gay in a lot of these texts. Perhaps this is a reflection of Roman position towards homosexuality, which was often more liberal than the rabbinic approach. That being said, Esau is depicted here as bottoming, something the Romans themselves had a tendency to look down on. In any case, it’s disconcerting and I personally do not like it.

A midrash first found in Midrash Tanḥuma Ḥukat 18:1 suggests that the king of ‘Arad mentioned in Numbers 21:1 was ‘Amaleq. Another midrash found in Midrash Aggadah Numbers 21:1 and repeated by Rashi suggests that this was because the ‘Amaleqites changed their speech and clothing to appear as Canaanites, so that if Israel prayed to defeat the Canaanites their prayers would not work.
Another name for Gideon or Jerubbaal, who fought with the ‘Amaleqites in their alliance with Midian in Judges 6 and 7.
According to Midrash Tanḥuma, Ki Tetzei 9:1, commenting on I Samuel 15:32-33, Shmuel cut pieces off Agag’s flesh and fed them to ostriches
David, referencing the narrative in II Samuel 1.
Referring to the battle against Ammon in II Chronicles 20 at “Ḥatzetzon Tamar, that is, Ein Gedi,” as well as Genesis 14:4 which states that th “field of the ‘Amaleqites” was in Ḥatzetzon Tamar.

A midrash found in the fifth petiḥta to Esther Rabbah, as well as in Rav Saadia Gaon’s commentary on Ezra 4:6, states that Shimshai, the scribe who sent slander against Israel to prevent them from building the Temple, was a son of Haman. The Hebrew word for “sun” is shemesh.
Haman, who weighted out ten thousand talents as a bribe to the king.
According to B. Megillah 15b, Haman had two hundred and eight sons, the gematria of וְרֹ֣ב in Esther 5:11.
Days. Bereshit Rabbah 100:6 points out that between Haman’s letter sent out on 13 Nisan and Mordechai’s letter on 23 Sivan was exactly seventy days.

Psalms 118:15. An acrostic of the five words in this verse — ק֤ׄוֹל ׀ רִׄנָּ֬ה וִׄישׁוּעָ֗ה בְּׄאׇהֳלֵ֥י צַׄדִּיקִ֑ים — are used as a backronym for the term קרובץ used in Ashkenazi practice to refer to the piyyuṭim added to the ‘amidah on Purim. This is a false etymology — it is actually just a derivation of קרובות. But it shows the links between this verse and Purim, despite the fact that this verse, as part of the Hallel service, is not actually said on Purim!
